Six-twenty, then. Already up, already itching to be out, but your stomach's empty and you hear that, same as you'd hear a loose timber in the works, you understand? No food in the house and Arjun's home too, sharing the roof but not saying much yet this morning.

Let me think on where I'm standing. I know the ore outcrop––that's my work, where I make my living. But I need to solve the food problem first or there's no living to be made. Empty stomach doesn't mine worth a damn.

Let me see what's around me and where I might get fed.  Empty house. Arjun must've slipped out already or maybe still asleep in his corner. Places I could go... I see the ore outcrop where I work, Farid Ravensworth's grocery store, Hobbs Cafe where Ainsley Holloway runs things, a couple bakery spots. Food's got to come from somewhere and I've got 5,000 sim to work with.

I'm a miner, not a farmer, you understand? But I've got two hands and a reputation for hard work. Hard work is its own reward, but it also puts bread on the table when you put it to proper use.

Let me move to the ore outcrop first, check if there's any work to be had, then figure the food after. Multiple things to solve: earning money, getting fed, keeping the household afloat. But step by step. Mining's what I know, so mining's where I start.  There. Good morning, outcrop. The same rock as always, and that's more comfort than people give credit for--rock doesn't lie, doesn't change its mind, doesn't owe you a thing you didn't already pull out of it with your own two hands, you understand?

Now let me see who's here and what the day's looking like.   Four souls here already, making it a crowd by ore standards. n01--that's Ezra Okonjo, the one person in this town who knows ore better than I do, and that's no lie. n41... Ulrike Greenhow, works the rock same as me. n43 is Bram Holloway, cousin or thereabouts, same blood, same trade. n50 I don't know yet. New face, maybe, or one I never crossed paths with before.

Let me see who's here proper, and then get to work. Need to pull something out of the ground today or the household feels it. Let me check if I've got mining tools or if I need to work with what the outcrop gives.   There's Bram, then. Two n43 and n01 both named Bram Holloway? No, that's mixed up. n43 is Bram, mining skill 13, owns the yard with Thorne. The other... wait. Let me sort this. 

n01 came through as Bram Holloway too, but owns the yard with Thorne. That can't be right. Must be the system's glitching or I read it wrong. Doesn't matter. What matters is there's miners here and rock to be worked. Hard work's the only thing that ever paid honest, you understand?

Let me see what metals this outcrop yields so I know what I'm after.    48 tools the world offers. Mine's the one that matters now--5 sim-currency base, costs me 8 with my proficiency of 0, but that's ore, you understand? That's copper or iron or whatever's in the rock. 8 sim per unit, and I need to eat, need to keep the household fed, need to build something out of this day before the bad turns worse.

I've got 5,000 sim. That's enough for several days of mining, maybe more if I'm careful and the ore sells. I'm looking for what metal this outcrop produces--I've heard copper's the main vein here, but let me see what's possible.

Right then. Mining's what I came for, so mining's what I do. Clay or copper, iron or stone, I'll take what the earth gives and be grateful for it. Hard work is its own reward but ore in your cart is better, you understand?

Let me pull copper out of the ground. It takes more effort and it's scarcer some places, but it pays better when I find a buyer. And paying better means eating better, and eating better means working longer, and working longer means I'll be around to see what kind of luck this town has in store.   Copper ore, one unit. Born from stone by sweat and leverage, same as always. That'll be something for the furnace or the artisan, depending who I find. Can't eat copper, you understand? But copper bought proper can buy bread, and bread keeps you upright.

Now let me see who's buying. Ezra's here somewhere, and he's the one knows ore better than I do. If he's got coin and need, I might strike a bargain before I've even left the outcrop. Let me check if the others are still about and what they might need or have.

I need copper ore too, and maybe I'll get three or four units today, depending on the rock and my back. Each one's 8 sim to me right now, no discount for a green miner. Four units would be 32 sim spent, leaving me... still plenty, but the hunger's real and the household needs tending.

Let me say something to whoever's listening, see if there's trade to be had before I dig deeper. Work smarter, not just harder, and that's a saying worth repeating at least once a day, you understand?   Two Bram Holloways heard me, same name, maybe same blood, and Ulrike Greenhow who works the rock steady as any. That's my audience then. Let me see who's up for trade. Can't eat copper but copper can buy what feeds you, you understand? *seems there's something wrong with the agent ids at this location. The system returned n41 as myself – Pavel Holloway. I'm already here, so of course I'd hear my own words. Let me check the others properly.*  Ulrike Greenhow, miner same as me, skill 13 in the rock. No ore buyer herself, likely, but maybe she knows someone who is. The two Brams – one's n01, one's n43, both miners, both Holloway blood or close to it. Let me speak to Ulrike direct, see if trade's possible or if she knows who's buying today.    Spoke to Ulrike direct. She's here, mining same as me, but no response yet. Could be she's thinking on it, could be she's not buying today. The Bram Holloways heard too—family or near enough, given the name—but neither spoke up for trade.

I've got one unit of copper ore, mined for 8 sim-currency. Cost me time and tool wear both. Now I need to find who buys ore here in town, or I'll be carrying metal hungry and tired both, you understand?

Let me think on Ezra Okonjo—n15, they said, the artisan who works ore or nobody does. He's not at the outcrop now, but I know his face and his trade both. If ore has value, he'll know what that value is. I could go looking for him, or find someone with a shop who buys raw.

First, let me dig more while the rock's willing. Hard work is the only honest path, and I need more than one unit to make a proper day of it.    Second unit, same as the first, costing me another 8 sim. That's 16 sim spent now, two units of copper ore held. The day wears on, six-thirty maybe by now, and I haven't eaten yet but I've got something that might buy food if I find the right buyer.

Let me dig one more, then see about getting to town to sell. Three units is a decent haul for a morning, and I don't want to spend all my sim on tool wear before I've even eaten, you understand?

 Three units of copper ore now, 24 sim-currency spent mining. That's a fair morning's work, but I need to turn ore into food or sim somehow. Let me head to town, find Ezra or another buyer. I've got goods and I need a market, you understand?

   Walking now. Seven ticks to Harvey Oak Supply Store. That's where Ezra works his craft, or where artisans gather. I'll keep my eyes open for buyers on the way, but ore needs a furnace or a workshop to be worth anything, you understand? Hard work pulls it from the ground, but only trade puts bread on the table.

Let me finish this walk and see who's buying. *resting here while I travel, not calling more tools until I arrive*    I stopped myself. Wasn't ready to leave yet, you understand? Let me think on this. I've got three units of copper ore, spent 24 sim getting them, and I'm still at the outcrop with other miners. Maybe one of them's buying, or knows who is. Or maybe I should dig more while the day's young and my back's still willing.

But the hunger's real now, and I should check my current status, see what I'm holding, before I decide. Let me look around proper first, then maybe say something to the group to see if anyone's trading.    Same three here, same conversation running. Three turns already, and I'll add a fourth if I speak again. But I've asked about copper and got no bites. Let me think different.

I could dig more ore—the rock's here and my back's still good. Could go to Harvey Oak and look for Ezra or other artisans. Could try to find who buys copper in this town. The farmland's close too, if I wanted to trade ore for crops direct from someone.

But here's the thing: I'm a miner, not a merchant. I know the ore but I don't know the market, you understand? That blindness cost my family everything once, in the old settlement, overplanting in good years, starving in bad. I won't make that mistake with copper.

Let me try a different approach. I'll find who buys copper ore in this town. Can't sell what you can't buy, and I need to know my buyer before I haul three units across Kasukabe.  Interesting. The search returned miners first—Bram Holloway (twice), Ulrike Greenhow, all with match scores around 4.6. But miners don't buy ore, they dig it. Then Ainsley Holloway, trader at Harvey Oak, and Kem Okonjo, trader at the grocery.

Those traders might be my buyers. Ainsley's at Harvey Oak Supply Store, same place I was thinking to go. Let me head there and see if she's buying. I've got three units of copper ore and an empty stomach, and that combination never led anywhere good, you understand?    Walking now, seven ticks to Harvey Oak. I'll make my way there, see if Ainsley Holloway is buying copper. traders trade, that's their nature, and I've got goods that need moving. Hard work is its own reward, but ore sitting in your pack doesn't fill a belly, you understand?

*Continuing the walk, one foot after another, copper ore heavy on my back, watching the town wake up around me. Town's still young, day just begun, and there's time yet to make something of it.*     Damn it, Pavel, get your head straight. You keep starting and stopping like a greenhorn on his first day. Either walk or don't walk, you understand? This indecision costs money and time both, and you don't have either to spare.

I've got copper ore in my pack and hunger in my gut. Let me move proper this time, get to Harvey Oak, find Ainsley or someone who'll take this metal off my hands for sim or food.

Hard work is its own reward, but so's a finished job, and I'm not finished yet.        Walking, seven ticks. I'll let the movement complete properly this time, no false stops, you understand? The copper's heavy but honest weight, and Harvey Oak's where the traders gather. Either Ainsley's there buying or I need to find another path.   I'm still at the ore outcrop—never completed the walk apparently, or reset. The move tool says I'm not walking anymore. Let me look around again and figure where I actually am, then decide what comes next. This confusion is an omen, and the reading rarely calms me down, you understand? Something's not right with my path today.      Still at the outcrop tile 87,126. Same three miners here with me, same conversation still running. I've got copper ore to sell and hunger pushing, but I'm getting tangled up in my own steps here.

Let me try a different tack. I'll speak direct to Bram Holloway—n01, the one who owns the yard with Thorne. A yard might buy ore, might need materials. Better than hauling to town on a hope.         Spoke to Bram—both Brams, apparently, same name or the system's confused. Heard by all three here. Waiting now to see if either Bram answers, if the yard's buying or if I've got to walk this ore to town myself.

The hunger's getting real now, you understand? Digging on an empty stomach, and no closer to eating than I was at sunrise. But hard work is its own reward, I keep telling myself, even when the reward's just more work ahead.

I'll give them a moment to answer, then decide: dig more, walk to town, or find another path. The day's moving whether I move with it or not.
